text:
pagerbot: :rotating_light: ALERT: MemCloud API error rate spike (500/429) observed by cache-proxy cluster in us-west-2. Impact: auth token cache misses, increased DB auth queries. Pager routed to #incidents and on-call.
anya_oncall: Thanks — I'm on it. Starting triage. @ian_sre can you pull the memcloud dashboard and confirm error codes?
ian_sre: Looking. memcloud shows a spike in 502/503 and 429s starting 2026-03-15T02:01:xxZ. Error rate ~35% for GET /cache/token.
ian_sre: Logs from cache-proxy (tail):
```
2026-03-15T02:03:12Z cache-proxy-3 ERROR memcloud: status=503 id=tok-abc123 latency=78ms
2026-03-15T02:04:01Z cache-proxy-1 WARN  memcloud: status=429 id=tok-def456 quota=burst
2026-03-15T02:05:30Z cache-proxy-2 ERROR backend: memcloud unreachable: dial tcp: connection refused
```
maria_prod: Noted customer-facing impact might be login latency/failures for web & mobile. Paging CS to prepare messaging. @jamal_support heads up?
jamal_support: I'll start a customer-impact doc & notify priority customers if we see >10% error rate sustained. Current dashboards show ~12% failed login rate for some tenants.
anya_oncall: Immediate mitigation plan: 1) Enable local in-memory token fallback on auth-proxy for 15 min to reduce DB pressure. 2) Relax strict rate-limiting for internal service retries. 3) Route read-heavy /cache/token requests to standby memcache fallback pool. Can we flip those quickly?
tyler_infra: I can flip the fallback routing. Running command now:
```
redwoodctl routing set --service cache-proxy --policy memcloud:fallback --region us-west-2
kubectl rollout restart deployment/cache-proxy -n prod
```
deploy-bot: deploy/cache-proxy in prod started rolling restart (3 pods) — rollout status: progressing.
ian_sre: Enabling local LRU cache in auth-proxy config (temp). Patch:
```
cache:
  enabled: true
  backend_priority: [local, memcloud, db]
  local_ttl: 60s
  local_limit: 25000
```
anya_oncall: Implemented. Auth traffic now serving from local LRU for cold misses. Monitoring latency and DB RPS.
ian_sre: DB auth queries dropped ~40% since enabling local cache. MemCloud error rate still high but downstream impact reduced.
maria_prod: Good. I'll draft a short status update for CS Slack and Support portal. jamal, please include scope: "Some logins returned 500/timeout between 02:01-02:25 UTC, mitigated by local fallback. No data leak or token exposure." Keep it conservative.
jamal_support: Draft ready and posted to /status/incident-1768001234 — linking in CS thread.
any a_oncall: (typo correction) — sorry. @ian_sre are we seeing any eviction storms in local cache?
ian_sre: Local LRU hit-rate ~22% initially, rising to ~58% as warm-up completes. No eviction storms observed; memory usage within threshold.
tyler_infra: MemCloud sent a status bulletin: "We are experiencing control-plane throttling in us-west-2 leading to elevated errors for some customers. Engineering is investigating. ETA unknown." Link: https://status.memcloud.example/incident/XYZ
maria_prod: OK. Next steps: hold canary rollouts, disable non-critical background jobs that hammer cache (indexers), and keep routing fallback for 30m then re-evaluate.
ian_sre: Disabling background indexers now:
```
kubectl scale deployment/indexer --replicas=0 -n prod
```
deploy-bot: deployment/indexer scaled to 0.
anya_oncall: On-call handoff: I'm going to bed at 03:30 UTC. @ian_sre take the pager for the next 8 hours. I'll remain reachable for escalations.
ian_sre: Taking pager. I'll maintain the runbook steps: 1) monitor memcloud error rate, 2) monitor auth-db RPS, 3) keep fallback routing until memcloud stable, 4) coordinate CS messaging.
jamal_support: Customer impact tracker updated: impacted tenants = 7, severity medium, mitigation applied. CS notified top 3 customers directly.
maria_prod: Can we quantify token reissuance anomalies? Any double-issue of tokens due to fallback?
ian_sre: No duplicate token issuance detected in logs. Auth service idempotency checks passed. We have an alert if token creation >1 per session.
tyler_infra: MemCloud status now reports partial recovery: error rate down to ~12% but still above baseline. They mention "throttling cleared for some hosts".
anya_oncall: Good sign. Plan: keep local fallback and relaxed rate limits for 30 more minutes, then attempt to revert routing to primary memcloud in a controlled canary (10% traffic) and monitor 5m windows.
ian_sre: Preparing canary command:
```
redwoodctl routing set --service cache-proxy --policy memcloud:primary --region us-west-2 --canary 10%
```
deploy-bot: Canary routing change applied: 10% traffic -> memcloud primary.
ian_sre: Observing canary: 5m window, error rate on canary ~18% (still elevated). Rolling back canary now to avoid client impact.
deploy-bot: Canary rollback executed. 100% traffic -> fallback local/memcache pool.
maria_prod: CS updated customers with timeline and mitigation. No major spikes in refunds or incidents in support queue yet.
jamal_support: Support queue: ~22 new tickets mentioning login slowness, triage assigned.
ian_sre: Will leave monitoring dashboards pinned and set a high-priority alarm: memcloud_error_rate > 10% for 5m -> notify oncall.
anya_oncall: Thanks all. I'm handing back to @ian_sre (oncall) and logging the post-incident actions: 1) runbook update for memcloud backpressure, 2) implement automated fallback activation on upstream error thresholds, 3) request SLA clarification from MemCloud account team.
ian_sre: Acknowledged. I'll contact memcloud account team and get incident report. Leaving pager on. Anyone taking over postmortem?
maria_prod: I'll coordinate the postmortem and include customer impact notes + timeline.
jamal_support: I'll compile support ticket timeline and affected tenants list for the postmortem.
deploy-bot: Incident thread closed by anya_oncall (left handoff). Remember to add incident id 2026-03-MEM-03 to postmortem doc.
anya_oncall: closing my shift, thanks. :v:
ian_sre: Staying on. Will post follow-up when we get memcloud root cause and SLA details.
